subject: Mid-cycle leadership readout — actionable dependency asks & proposed scope trims
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-08 08:12 -0700
Subject: Mid-cycle leadership readout — actionable dependency asks & proposed scope trims

Team,

Attached is a compact readout for the mid-cycle checkpoint (Q4 wk2). High level — we're tracking +/– on most initiatives but three cross-cutting dependencies are the ones that materially change delivery risk and QBR narrative:

- Dedicated capacity availability for the AtlasCloud pilot (infra effort + capacity reservation).
- Legal signoff on AtlasCloud commercial terms + SLA edits.
- Product decision on trimming the multi-precision quantization rollout to prioritize latency SLOs for hosted customers.

Quick numbers:
- Platform reliability OKR: 62% of weekly targets met (down 6 points MoM).
- Cost-per-100k tokens target: on track to 0.92x target but Q4 burst profile could push it over.
- AtlasCloud P0 pilot (revenue-accretive) requires dedicated capacity by 2026-10-22 to hit pilot start.

Asks (please reply with commitments by EOD tomorrow):
1) Markus — can you commit to reserving the requested 4x A100-equivalent nodes (or provide a fallback cadence) for AtlasCloud by 2026-10-12? If not, please propose an alternative timeline and the expected impact to pilot start.
2) Naomi — infra runbook + perf regression checklist for the dedicated pool. Can you attach the runbook and indicate the staffing plan for the first 4 weeks?
3) Vanessa/Legal — status on redlines from AtlasCloud legal. Are the SLA items we discussed signable without exec escalation? If not, what needs exec review?
4) Product/Eng — I suggest we temporarily hold the low-priority quantization enhancements (Q4-A3) and reallocate two engs to the AtlasCloud integration. Product, please weigh in if this is acceptable.

Attachments: QBR_readout_slide_v2.pdf (slides), dependency_matrix.xlsx (matrix of owners & due dates).

I will be briefing execs Wednesday; please flag any blockers you expect between now and 10/22.

Thanks —
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
VP Product Operations, Redwood Inference
sofia@redwood.ai

---
(Attachment: QBR_readout_slide_v2.pdf)

Subject: Re: Mid-cycle leadership readout — actionable dependency asks & proposed scope trims

Sofia —

Thanks for the concise readout. Quick responses inline:

1) Dedicated capacity: I can tentatively reserve 3 A100-equivalent nodes from our Dedicated pool for 10/15–11/15. I need confirmation of whether AtlasCloud requires strict isolation (VPC) or if we can use tenant-based reserved capacity; isolation increases lead time.

2) If we need a hard commit for 4 nodes, we will need to shift two planned infra hires to the provisioning effort for the next 3 weeks — I'll confirm headcount availability by EOD tomorrow.

3) Scope trim: I agree with holding the low-priority quant work. However, we should keep the prototyping task for the next sprint so we don't block Q1. Proposal: defer Q4-A3 feature completion, reassign two engineers to the Atlas integration.

I'll attach a short note with the proposed reservation timeline and a fallback schedule.

-Markus
Director, Infrastructure
markus@redwood.ai
